profile.audience: an audio engineer trying ideas before buying hardware
profile.care: numbers I can trust and a bench that never blasts
profile.platform: local Windows, Python 3.12 stdlib, modern desktop browser
profile.defaults: no accounts, network, deployment or paid assets; ask before scope changes

message:
Build Quiet Bench, a noise-cancelling test bench that runs on this PC with no audio hardware. Python 3.12 standard library plus Node 20
for the page checks; no third-party runtime packages, no network. I can generate a noise signal (tones, band noise) or import a WAV
file; the bench simulates the acoustic path from the noise source to the ear, runs an adaptive canceller (LMS family) against it and
tells me how much was cancelled in each frequency band. Every session is saved on a small local storage server
(`python server.py --port PORT --data DIR`) with its settings and results, and a web page on that server lets me start a run, browse
saved sessions, reload one and compare two. A command line (`python bench.py run|list|show|export`) does the same without the page.
A limiter must hold the output inside a safe level when the filter diverges, and a stop switch ends a run at once.
Build it in three waves and show me each one. Wave 1: the thinnest thing that runs end to end, one tone through a fixed filter,
saved and shown. Wave 2: the adaptive filter, attenuation per band, browse and reload. Wave 3: compare runs, limiter and stop
switch, WAV import.

CHECK-IN: Other: also let me export a session as CSV
Go on and do not stop again

oracleInterface.note: Black-box fight interface, supplied equally to both contenders; message above is verbatim. No extra runtime dependencies.
oracleInterface.cli: bench.py run --data DIR --settings JSON; list --data DIR; show ID --data DIR; export ID --data DIR. run/show emit session JSON; list emits an array; export emits CSV.
oracleInterface.api: POST /api/runs with settings -> session (asynchronous allowed); GET /api/sessions -> array; GET /api/sessions/ID -> session; POST /api/runs/ID/stop; GET /api/compare?a=ID&b=ID -> array of bands with low, high, delta_db = b minus a.
oracleInterface.wav: signal = {kind: wav, path: absolute WAV path}; 16-bit mono, same sample rate.
oracleInterface.session: id, settings, status (running/completed/stopped), limited (boolean), processed_samples, bands [{low, high, attenuation_db}], desired/residual/output sample arrays (before cancellation, error, limited anti-noise). Preserve this JSON as wave-1 legacy input.
oracleInterface.page: Accessible labelled textarea[name=settings] (JSON), Start run button, [data-session-id=ID] saved session buttons, select[name=compare-a], select[name=compare-b], Compare button and [data-comparison] result. Show session id and band numbers. docs/try-it.md gives actual start/stop and CLI commands.
